novel_features.name: Scheduled send queue
novel_features.description: Write an email now and have it sent at any future time, even though the Gmail API itself has no schedule-send. Delivery requires `schedule run` from cron/launchd (or `schedule run --watch`).
novel_features.rationale: Gmail's schedule-send is UI-only; a local SQLite outbox plus a due-time processor builds the missing capability with idempotent, never-double-send semantics.
novel_features.example: gmail-pp-cli schedule send --to prospect@example.com --subject "Following up" --body-file pitch.txt --at "2026-08-04T09:00:00"
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever a user asks to send an email later, at a specific time, or in another timezone; no other Gmail API tool can do it. Tell the user to wire `gmail-pp-cli schedule run` into cron, or the queue will sit undelivered.

novel_features.name: Sender leaderboard
novel_features.description: See who actually fills your mailbox: per-sender message count, unread count, total size, and first/last seen.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a GROUP BY over the entire synced mailbox in local SQLite; the live API would need tens of thousands of quota-metered fetches to answer it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before any cleanup or unsubscribe pass to rank which senders matter; the live API cannot aggregate by sender at all. Requires a populated local mirror: run `gmail-pp-cli pull` first.

novel_features.name: Storage hogs
novel_features.description: Rank senders and years by mailbox bytes consumed, with the exact cleanup command printed next to each group.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates synced sizeEstimate locally and pairs every group with a ready-to-run find query and batch cleanup invocation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the user is near their storage quota or asks what is taking up space in Gmail. Requires a populated local mirror: run `gmail-pp-cli pull` first.

novel_features.name: Follow-up tracker
novel_features.description: List threads where the last word was theirs (you owe a reply) or yours (they never replied), aged past N days.
novel_features.rationale: A SQL window query over local threads, messages, and sendAs identities; via the live API this is a per-thread fetch storm at 20 quota units per message.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for outreach chasing (who never replied) and inbox accountability (what do I owe); no Gmail search operator can express either. Requires a populated local mirror: run `gmail-pp-cli pull` first.

novel_features.name: Unsubscribe audit
novel_features.description: Rank mailing lists by volume and unread ratio, and emit each list's unsubscribe target ready to act on.
novel_features.rationale: Joins stored List-Unsubscribe headers with per-sender stats from the local store; Gmail exposes the header only one message at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the user wants to cut inbox noise; the unread ratio identifies lists they never actually read. Requires a populated local mirror: run `gmail-pp-cli pull` first.

novel_features.name: Filters as code
novel_features.description: Keep Gmail filters in a version-controlled YAML file; diff against live settings and apply the reconciliation plan.
novel_features.rationale: Three-way diff between a declarative file and the live filter list with a dry-run plan, absorbing gmailctl's niche without its Jsonnet complexity.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when the user manages filters across machines or wants filter changes reviewed before they touch the account.

narrative.headline: Every Gmail API surface plus the things Gmail itself will not give you: scheduled sends, sender analytics, follow-up tracking, and an offline full-text mailbox.
narrative.value_prop: gmail-pp-cli mirrors your mailbox into local SQLite with gmail-pp-cli pull (incremental history sync), so search, sender leaderboards, storage analytics, and follow-up tracking run instantly and cost zero quota. It also fills the API's biggest gap with a local scheduled-send queue, and ships agent-native output on every command.
narrative.auth_narrative: Gmail uses OAuth2. Run `gmail-pp-cli auth login` once: it opens a browser consent flow using OAuth client credentials supplied via --client-id/--client-secret, the GMAIL_CLIENT_ID / GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET environment variables, or an interactive prompt. Tokens are stored locally and refresh automatically. For headless use, set GMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN to a pre-minted token.

quickstart.comment: Verify the binary, config, and auth wiring before touching the API
Live Gmail search with the same operators as the Gmail search box
Mirror recent mail (headers plus decoded bodies) into local SQLite so analytics and offline search work
Unread summary grouped by sender and category
Who fills your mailbox: counts, unread, and size per sender from the local store

troubleshoots.fix: Enable the Gmail API for your GCP project: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/gmail.googleapis.com then retry

troubleshoots.symptom: invalid_grant or token expired after 7 days
troubleshoots.fix: Your OAuth consent screen is in Testing mode; publish the app or re-run gmail-pp-cli auth login to re-consent
Re-run gmail-pp-cli pull with a narrower window such as --since 7d; the client backs off automatically and the saved history cursor resumes incrementally

troubleshoots.symptom: search or senders returns nothing but find works
troubleshoots.fix: Local analytics need a populated mirror; run gmail-pp-cli pull --since 30d first
The queue only fires while gmail-pp-cli schedule run is invoked (cron) or running with --watch; check gmail-pp-cli schedule list for pending items

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for gmail-pp-cli when an agent task involves reading, searching, sending, or cleaning up Gmail: triaging unread mail, replying with correct threading, scheduling a send for later, harvesting attachments, or answering mailbox-wide questions like who emails me most or what is eating my storage. The local SQLite mirror (populated by `gmail-pp-cli pull`) makes it the right choice for any question spanning more than a page of messages, where raw API calls would burn quota and context. Do not use it for non-Gmail mailboxes (Outlook, IMAP, Yahoo), for Google Calendar, Contacts, or Drive, for Workspace admin-console tasks such as managing users or org policies, or for drafting copy that is never going to be sent.

recipes.title: Morning triage
recipes.explanation: Unread mail grouped by sender and category in compact agent-shaped JSON, ready for a summarize-and-archive loop.

recipes.title: Narrow a live list for an agent
recipes.command: gmail-pp-cli messages list me --q "has:attachment newer_than:7d" --agent --select messages.id,messages.threadId
recipes.explanation: Typed endpoint call with dotted-path field selection so the agent gets ids without the verbose envelope.

recipes.title: Schedule tomorrow's follow-up
recipes.command: gmail-pp-cli schedule send --to alex@example.com --subject "Re: proposal" --body-file followup.txt --in 18h
recipes.explanation: Queues the send locally; a cron-invoked schedule run fires it at the due time, exactly once.

recipes.title: Chase silent prospects
recipes.explanation: Sent threads where nobody replied in 3 days, from the local store at zero quota cost.

recipes.title: Cut inbox noise
recipes.explanation: Mailing lists ranked by volume and never-read ratio with their unsubscribe targets.
